 Wife of Sri Krishna Reddy,

 Son of Shri Durga Gowda,

JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That, on 25.11.2023 at about 6.30 p.m. the petitioner was pedestrian proceeding on Bengaluru- Bannerughatta main road, near Kalkere gate, Jigani Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District, at that time driver of the goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-51-ET-9942 moving from Benglauru towards Bannerghatta, slowly and cautiously and when he reached near Kalkere gate one goods vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AF-4758 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and then motor cycle again parked vehicle bearing No.KA-41-D-5286 &
KA-51-MS-3532.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Vinayaka Hospital, Bengaluru, then shifted to Sri Chandrashekara Hospital, Hosur, wherein she took the treatment as an inpatient and had spent huge amount towards medicines, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
4.
It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 53 years, doing coolie and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
After the accident, she could not do any work due to her severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the goods vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AF- 4758.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Bannerghatta police in Crime No.331/2023 under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition seeking compensation.
6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.
7. In the written statement of the respondent No.1, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

But he has contended that the accident was not occurred due to Narasamma vs Kumar D on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147075336/
2 the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Further stated that this respondent is the RC owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AF-4758 and the said vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 and the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
The driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exhorbitant, abnormal and without any legal and equitable basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of goods vehicle bearing No.KA-51- AF-4758 and its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also defence of the respondent that alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
And the vehicle had no valid fitness to ply in the place of accident.
It is also contention of the respondent that medical bills claimed by the petitioner are not paid by him and are not supported with the proper money receipts.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition.
Ultimately stated that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner, is highly excessive, exorbitant and without any basis.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3) What order or award?

10. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, she has placed her affidavit evidence in lieu of examination-in-chief, who examined as PW1 and got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
11.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined MRO of Chandrashekara Hospital, Hosur as RW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.

Further examined Legal Executive of the insurance company as RW2 and got marked the document at Ex.R3 & Ex.R4.
12.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

13. At the time of argument the counsel for the petitioner has relied the following decisions;
1) MFA No.101337/2021 C/W 101664/2021 between The Divisional Controller Vs. Smt.Bismilah &
Others Wherein the Hon'ble HighCourt of Karnataka held that "the discharge summary cannot be the sole basis to come to conclusion that the injury is caused due to slipping from the motor cycle".
Narasamma vs Kumar D on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147075336/
3 2) MFA No.8490/2010 between Kumari Fazeelath Vs.Mr.Zubair Ahmed & Another Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that "the FIR is followed by due investigation by the police in discharge of their official duties and in the absence of any material to discrete what the charge sheet says, there is a presumption of correctness of the original of the police u/s 114 R/W Section 32 of Indian Evidence Act, 1872 since the investigation is undertaken and regulated by the law."

14.My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:

R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:-
15.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-51-AF-4758, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

16. On the other hand, the respondents though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
17. In such a situation, burden is more on the part of the Tribunal to assess the evidence available on record, in order to come to the proper conclusion in connection with the above fact in issue.
18. The petitioner in order to prove his case, examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in- chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
Ex .P1 is the true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.331/2023 of Bannerghatta police Station.
Ex . P2
is the true copy of the first information statement given by Virendra.
Ex . P3
is the true copy of the 161 statement.
Ex . P4
is the true copy of the spot mahazar.
Ex . P5
is the true copy of the notice u/s 133 of MV Act
, Ex.P6 is the true copy of reply to notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Ex.
P7 & Ex.P8 is the true copy of IMV report, Ex.P9 is the true copy of the charge sheet in Crime No.331/2023 of Bannerghatta police.

19. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, the S.H.O. of Bannerghatta police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 & 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging Narasamma vs Kumar D on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147075336/
4 that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
20.
In order to substantiate its contention, the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Executive as RW2.
He has deposed in his evidence that as per medical records the history of accident is 'hit by two wheeler,'.
The petitioner has made false complaint against the goods vehicle bearing No.KA-51-AF-4758.
The jurisdictional police have filed false charge sheet against the driver of the goods vehicle.
Hence, there is no involvement of the offending vehicle.
He has placed authorisation letter and policy copy as per Ex.R3 & Ex.R4.
In the cross-examination he has denied the suggestion that as per Ex.P11 immediately after the accident on 25.11.2023, the petitioner was taken treatment at Vinayaka Hospital.

Further admitted that the accident occurred on 25.11.2023.
21.
Further examined MRO of Sri Chandrashekar Hospital, Hosur as RW1.
He has deposed in his evidence that generally in RTA cases their hospital is maintaining MLC register.
In this case, there is no MLC because there was 11 days delay before taking admission to their hospital.
In Ex.P12 history of RTA is mentioned as hit by two wheeler.
In the cross-examination he has admitted that petitioner took the treatment in another hospital before admitting to their hospital.
The petitioner came to their hospital only for general check up.

Though the respondents have disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, but not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any independent eye witness to prove their defence.
22. The PW1 was subjected for cross- examination, but nothing has been elicited from his mouth to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

23. In the light of the discussions held above, it is crystal clear that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligendriving of the driver of the goods vehicle beairng No.KA-51-AF- 4758.
In the said accident, the petitioner had sustained injuries.

Hence, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative ISSUE No.2 :
24.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by her in the accident under different heads.

25. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by her,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.

The compensation should Narasamma vs Kumar D on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147075336/
5 not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in her evidence that, she has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries she has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P9.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Incise wound over right lower limb 2) Abrasion over right glutel region 3) Lacerated wound over scalp and both knee joint 27.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are simple in nature.

Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries issued by Vinayaka Hospital, Bengaluru & Sri. Chandrashekara Hospital, Hosur, at Ex.P11 & Ex.P12, which shows that he was admitted from 25.11.2023 to 27.11.2023 & from 4.12.2023 to 7.12.2023.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor.
Except production of these documents she has not placed any other documents to show that she has sustained grievous injuries.
By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner.
It is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
28.
PW1 has stated that, she was doing coolie and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
she has not placed any iota of documents to show his income per month.

In such a situation, as per law,
notional income has to be taken.

The petitioner has produced discharge summaries issued by Vinayaka Hospital, Bengaluru & Sri. Chandrashekara Hospital, Hosur, at Ex.P11 & Ex.P12, which shows that he was admitted from 25.11.2023 to 27.11.2023 & from 4.12.2023 to 7.12.2023.
But as per the wound certificate, she sustained only simple injuries at least she could have taken rest for little period.
By taking into consideration of the said aspect, I am of the view that, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.
The petitioner in connection with her treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence, placed medical bills of Rs.51,440/- as per Ex.P14 along with prescriptions at Ex.P13.
Except the suggestion there are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medica bills.

Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.51,440/- towards medical expenses Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
30.
The petitioner herein, as per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained only simple injuries.
The petitioner took the treatment as an inpatient from 25.11.2023 to 27.11.2023 & from 4.12.2023 to 7.12.2023.

The petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment,
conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
Loss of future income;

31. Except the production of wound certificate and discharge summary and averments made in the main petition as well as in the chief affidavit, has not made an effort to examine the treated doctor,
in order to prove the disability sustained by her, due to the accidental injuries in order to know,
whether the injuries sustained by the petitioner will effect to her future, and whether the said injuries will make any discomfort to the petitioner to do her routine work as well as her work for his avocation.
In such a situation, court cannot consider the loss of future income, in the absence of convincing evidence from the side of the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for the compensation under the head of loss of future Income due to want of evidence on record.

Loss of amenities;
32. PW1 has stated in her evidence that due to the accidental injuries she is unable to sit, stand, walk for a while, limping while walking and not active as before.

On going through the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate submitted by the petitioner herein and also in the light of the entire facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,000/- towards loss of amenities.
33. In connection with the future medication, the petitioner has not placed any documents in this regard for consideration.
Hence, I am of the view that, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of future medication.

34. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs.15,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs.10,000-00 laid-up period and rest period Narasamma vs Kumar D on 4 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147075336/
7
3 . Medical expenses Rs.51,440-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 7,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Nil due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 3,000-00 7.
Future medication Nil Total Rs.86,440-00 35.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.86,440/- (Rupees eighty six thousand four hundred and forty only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016, between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

sentences.text: , from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
36.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Goods vehicle bearing registration No.KA-51-AF-4758 alleged accident had taken place.
As such, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
37. As per Ex.R4, the policy was valid from 27.1.2023 to 26.1.2024.
The alleged accident was taken place on 25.11.2023.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.1 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
38.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.86,440/- (Rupees eighty six thousand four hundred and forty only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.
